items.title: 3 Dividend Stocks That Could Hold Up Better As Rates Stay Higher
items.summary: Rising US Treasury yields near 5.25%, an expensive oil market linked to the US–Iran war, and stubborn 3.7% inflation are squeezing many high‑valuation stocks, yet cash‑rich dividend payers can sometimes feel the pressure less intensely. Income hunters who ignore this shift risk missing opportunities in quieter corners of the market. items.title: Can Tyson Foods Keep Paying Its Dividend While Beef Bleeds Money?
items.summary: Beef is bleeding hundreds of millions in losses while Tyson's stock slides, yet the company keeps writing dividend checks without flinching. Whether that confidence is earned or reckless depends on what you look at first.

items.title: Hormel Foods vs General Mills: One Dividend Rests on Solid Cash, the Other on Fumes
items.summary: Both Hormel and General Mills paid out more in dividends than they earned last year, but that shared screener flag tells a completely different story at each company. One dividend sits on solid footing while the other is quietly running out of room.
